messages:
sam: Heads-up: after the kernel-selection tweak this morning, short-chat p95 jumped ~2x on host-side paths. Small requests (<=128 tokens) are seeing tail latency ~140ms vs ~70ms before. Link to perf: https://perf.redwood/reports/477777
lucy: ugh. is this happening on both dedicated and hosted infra?
sam: repros on dedicated canaries and hosted-west. Only obvious delta is kernel selection change + new batching hint. I attached a flamegraph from the canary.
sam: ```
# flame summary (short requests)
- host-ingress: 36% (tokenize + parse)
- streaming-assembler: 24% (serialize/flush)
- kernel-dispatch: 22% (overhead increased)
- kvcache: 8% (miss rate up)
```
nate: can you paste the exact kernel selector config we rolled? maybe it's forcing a kernel that does extra serialization for small seqs
sam: selector: "auto-v2" with hint smaller_batch_strategy=hold-10ms. We lowered kernel threshold to prefer fused-attn for medium seqs.
marco: hold-10ms can backpressure host-streaming. It batches more but also delays flushing; for short requests that looks like added latency.
lucy: but why tokenize time doubled? that's upstream of batching
sam: profiler shows tokenization now doing additional copy at frame boundary. Looks like new proto framing change + http2 writev path caused a memcpy on every chunk. snippet from logs:
sam: ```
Wrote 1 frame, copying 2048 bytes to proto buffer (was zero-copy)
```
perf-bot: regression-alert: short_request_p95 increased 98% in canary (477777-08) — traces available
nate: hypothesis: kernel-selection change altered request routing -> different ingress proxy path that triggers proto-copy fallback on grpc v2. That explains both tokenize and streaming spikes.
marco: quick experiment: flip selector back for canary and disable hold-10ms batching. Want to see which change is dominant.
sam: running canary rollback now. Also uploading full trace and kvcache hit stats.
sam: kvcache: miss rate for short keys jumped from 4% -> 15% after change. Might be because batching changed request coalescing keys.
lucy: interesting — if batching groups requests differently KV keys may become more fragmented, increasing misses. Could amplify backend tail.
nate: actionables: 1) rollback selector in canary (marco) 2) run A/B with hold-10ms off (sam) 3) capture writev vs copy counts on ingress (lucy) 4) derive kvcache key grouping metric (perf-bot)
marco: started rollback, will update in ~5m :thumbsup:
sam: thanks. if rollback fixes p95 we'll iterate on batching hints + avoid proto-copy path. Also add small-request focused KV coalescing rule.
lucy: can we add lightweight unit test to catch zero-copy->copy regressions? a small harness that asserts writev path used for fragments
nate: yes, I'll add that to the ingress test suite.
marco: rollback complete on canary. baseline p95 down to ~75ms. still running full sweep.
sam: initial signal looks good. leaving this thread open while we collect diffs.
marco: update: kvcache miss rate trending back to 5% on canary. Looks like selector rollback fixed coalescing. closing loop after full sweep.
sam: awesome. follow-ups: propose removing hold-10ms default and add opt-in, plus add ingress writev telemetry and a kvcache-grouping unit test.
lucy: noted, will create tickets.
perf-bot: ticket created: PERF-1328 (ingress-writev-metrics), PERF-1329 (kv-coalescing-test), PERF-1330 (remove-hold-10ms-default)
sam: cool — thanks everyone.
